item.title: Meet Our Pathway to Publishing Fellow: Ariana Benson
item.description: Ariana Benson is a poet-storyteller from Chesapeake, Virginia. A graduate of Spelman College and Royal Holloway University of London, where she studied Poetic Practice as a 2019 Marshall Scholar, she received the 2021 Graybeal-Gowen Prize and was a finalist for the 2020 Auburn Witness Poetry Prize and the 2021 Pink Poetry Prize. item.title: The Power of Words and the Leap of Faith: Our Journey with Wise Ink
item.description: In 2013, we took a leap of faith, fueled by a shared dream and a few scribbled napkins. What began as a simple blog, Wise Ink, has since grown into a thriving community where authors find their voice and their purpose. Our journey started with fear, joy, and a belief that stories can change the world. Now, Wise Ink stands as a testament to the power of words—and the courage to follow where they lead.

item.title: Storytelling for Social Impact: How Personal Narratives Spark Collective Change
item.description: Successful community organizing starts with storytelling. Attorney and disability advocate Lola Dada-Olley shares how the gains won by the disability rights movement over the last four decades have largely occurred because of neurodivergent people and their families sharing their stories in their communities. While they may have started to improve their lives and the lives of their families, their legacy has improved the lives of many for generations to come.

item.title: When Your Book Gets Banned: Authorship During Censorship
item.description: Julie Lyford, activist and award-winning author, has had her books banned and even burned for featuring stories with LGBTQ+ characters. She shares an honest look at the current landscape of heightened censorship and how she plans to move forward.
